intro: An aluminium extruder in Vietnam that finishes, fabricates and ships what it draws.

chapters.name: Company
chapters.title: Drawn, finished and packed in one place
chapters.lede: Everything we sell is drawn, finished and packed in Vietnam. That is a commercial position, not a sentiment.
body: Böss Group extrudes, finishes and fabricates aluminium in Vietnam. The aluminium plant, Hoàng Kim, has been in operation since 2013, and aluminium door and facade systems have been part of the range since it opened.

Keeping extrusion, anodising, powder coating and fabrication under one roof is the reason a customer can order a complete window system rather than a bundle of bars. It also means that when a colour has to be matched two years after the first delivery, the matching is done on the line that made the original, against a retained sample, rather than negotiated between three subcontractors.

Export buyers do not all ask the same question first. European enquiries tend to open on thermal performance and recycled content; Australian ones on cyclonic rating and coastal exposure; buyers closer to home ask about price and how fast a truck can get there. The specification that follows is different in each case, and it is cheaper to say so at the enquiry than at the first delivery.

chapters.name: Capability
chapters.title: What the plants can actually do
chapters.lede: Extrusion, then the finishing capacity to keep up with it — which is the part that usually does not keep up.
body: Presses run across a range of tonnages, and that range is what sets both the largest section a plant can draw and the smallest it can draw economically. Dies are cut and corrected in house. The correction loop after the first sample is the difference between a section that holds tolerance across a full billet and one that holds it for the first three metres, and it is work that cannot be bought in by the hour.

Finishing is where most extruders under-invest. We run anodising and powder coating on site, sized against the presses rather than against last year's order book, so a finished order does not wait behind an unfinished one.

Fabrication covers cutting, CNC machining, punching, welding and assembly. Facade units are glazed and water-tested before they ship, which moves the difficult work off the scaffold and into a building where it can be repeated.

chapters.name: History
chapters.title: 2013 to now
chapters.lede: The aluminium business starts at one plant in 2013. The group it belongs to is older than that, and was making something else.
body: The Hoàng Kim aluminium plant went into operation in 2013. That is where this business starts, and aluminium door systems and curtain walling entered the range with it.

The group itself goes back much further and grew up in doors and shutters rather than in extrusion. It is worth saying plainly, because a founding date on an About page is usually read as the date the people in the photographs started doing the thing they are photographed doing, and here those are two different dates.

In 2025 the group took a single name, Böss Group, in place of the separate marks its businesses had traded under. The plant kept doing what it had been doing; what changed was the name on the paperwork.

chapters.name: Quality
chapters.title: What we are certified to, and what that means
chapters.lede: Certification is not a claim about our products. It is a claim that we can prove what happened to them.
body: The group holds ISO 9001. That is the certification listed on this page; for anything your specification names, ask us for a current copy and check it against the issuing body's register. A certificate named on a website and a certificate current in the register are two different things, and the second is the one that matters when a project is audited.

Behind any certificate is the part that takes longest to build: traceability. A finished profile should resolve to its billet lot, its alloy certificate, its die history, its coating batch and the test results for that batch. That chain is what a quality system is for; the certificate is only the evidence that someone checked the chain.

Testing is done on site — salt spray, accelerated weathering, coating thickness and adhesion, and water penetration on facade units. Send us the hold points and acceptance criteria your specification needs and we will tell you which we run in house and which we would arrange. Where a project requires third-party witness testing we arrange it rather than substituting our own results for it.

chapters.name: Impact
chapters.title: Aluminium is recyclable; that is not the same as recycled
chapters.lede: Remelting aluminium takes about five per cent of the energy of making it from ore. What matters is how much of what you are buying actually came from remelt.
body: Recyclability is a property of the metal, and every extruder in the world can claim it. Recycled content is a property of a particular billet lot, and it moves from lot to lot depending on what scrap was available that month. The two get used interchangeably in marketing, and a specification that asks for the first has asked for nothing.

The useful question to put to any supplier, including us, is narrower: what was the recycled content of the billet in this order, was it post-industrial or post-consumer, and what document says so. Post-industrial scrap — extrusion offcuts returned and remelted — is the easy half. Post-consumer is the hard half, because the alloy has to be verified before it can go back into a structural section.

We quote recycled content per order, against the mill certificate for that billet, rather than as a group average. An average is the one number guaranteed not to describe the delivery in front of you.

Anodising rinse water and coating pretreatment are the other two places where an aluminium plant either spends money or moves a problem downstream. Ask what happens to both; the answer is specific to a plant and to a year, which is why it belongs in a reply to an enquiry rather than on a page that stays up.

chapters.name: Careers
chapters.title: Work with us
chapters.lede: Die design, metallurgy, coating chemistry, facade engineering. The people we struggle to hire are the ones who have done it on a line, not only on a drawing.
body: The technical roles are die design, metallurgy, coating chemistry, quality and facade engineering. Extrusion is unusual in that the drawing and the line are the same problem: a die that is elegant on screen and slow to correct on the press costs more than a plain one that runs.

Apprentices rotate through extrusion, finishing and fabrication, and the rotation includes a spell in quality. Putting apprentices through quality is deliberate: someone who has measured coating thickness for a few months operates a coating line differently afterwards, and no amount of instruction produces the same effect.

Engineering graduates rotate through more than one part of the plant before they settle. We sponsor final-year projects on die correction and on extrusion of high-recycled-content billet, which is where our own open problems are — the sponsorship is not outreach, it is us buying attention on something we have not solved.
